name: Demand Excellence
definition: Leaders have a passion for excellence and do not tolerate mediocrity. We hold ourselves and others to a high standard that we raise perpetually.

rows.situation: When the work is fine and not good
rows.under: Approves it. Nobody wants the conversation.
rows.justRight: Says exactly what is missing and what good would look like, then expects it.
rows.over: Sends work back over things no customer or colleague would ever notice.

rows.situation: When the standard has quietly dropped
rows.under: Adapts to the new normal without noticing it moved.
rows.justRight: Names the drift, restates the bar, and holds the next piece of work to it.
rows.over: Raises the bar so often mid-project that nothing can ever be finished.

rows.situation: When the work below the bar is yours
rows.under: Applies the standard to others and not to yourself.
rows.justRight: Holds your own work to the bar first, and in public.
rows.over: Reworks your own output endlessly and becomes the bottleneck.

rows.situation: When excellence and the date conflict
rows.under: Lowers the standard silently to make the date.
rows.justRight: Decides openly which part must be excellent and which part can be good, and says why.
rows.over: Treats every part as equally critical and delivers nothing on time.

rows.under: Says nothing. The bar is the job.
rows.justRight: Names precisely what was excellent, so the standard becomes concrete for everyone.
rows.over: Praises so freely that the word excellent stops carrying information.

rows.situation: When everyone knows about the broken thing
rows.under: Routes around it. It has been broken so long that it feels permanent.
rows.justRight: Refuses to accept it. Fixes it, or gets it owned with a date.
rows.over: Stops all forward work to fix every known imperfection at once.
